S1.back: 5 free [ones, masculine plural, agreeing with the unspoken Cutlingai]
S1.why: Adjective in nominative plural, which is the right case after 2 to 9; the noun is left out because the five tiles above say what is free.

S2.why: An invitation in the polite jūs imperative the vocabulary uses; no word for limit or warning, and 19 characters fits the 20 budget.

S3.s: Panaudojote visus %lld nemokamus Cutlingus. Už juos mokėti nereikės, jie ir toliau veiks.
S3.back: You-used all 5 free Cutlings [accusative]. For them to-pay will-not-be-needed, they also further will-work.
S3.why: Accusative plural after visus 5 is correct for 2 to 9; the second sentence says plainly that those five stay free and keep working, in future tense so it reads as a promise.

S4.why: Future tense tells a new user what they get without the "you can" sentence; accusative plural agrees with 5; 45 characters with the digit filled in.

S5.back: Used [impersonal neuter] 3 out-of 5 free Cutlings [genitive plural].
S5.why: The neuter participle panaudota needs no agreement with the used count, and iš takes the genitive plural Cutlingų for any total from 2 up.

S6.why: Capacity genitive as in "salė 300 žmonių"; a round thousand takes the genitive plural Cutlingų, the form the vocabulary's count string already uses.

S7.back: Up-to 5 000 text and 500 image Cutlings [genitive plural].
S7.why: Builds on the vocabulary's own item names Teksto Cutlingas and Vaizdo Cutlingas, sharing one head noun; both round numbers take the genitive plural.

S8.why: Lithuanian lists three things with a comma and ir, no serial comma; device names stay unquoted, as Mac is in the vocabulary's "Cutling, skirtas Mac".

S9.s: Vienas pirkimas galioja visuose jūsų „Apple“ paskyros įrenginiuose.
S9.back: One purchase is-valid in-all your "Apple" account's devices.
S9.why: „Apple“ paskyra in Lithuanian quotes exactly as the vocabulary writes it; įrenginiuose carries the case so the brand names never need declining.

S10.why: A plain statement in the jūs present tense; vienkartinis pirkimas would be accurate but reads like a receipt.

S11.why: Be with three genitives is how a Lithuanian lists what is absent; reklama in the singular is the usual collective word for ads, and registracija is the word people use for signing up.

S12.why: The infinitive command form Lithuanian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action; pirkiniai matches the App Store's own Pirkiniai.

S13.why: Impersonal present participle, the standard progress form (like Įkeliama…, Atsisiunčiama…), with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Infinitive button form; Cutling stays undeclined as in the vocabulary; už plus the price is how a Lithuanian names what a button costs. 21 characters plus the price.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 with nothing after it, 9 characters within the 14 budget.

S16.why: The usual polite way to put something off in Lithuanian; it does not say no.

S17.why: The infinitive Lithuanian iOS puts on close buttons.

S18.why: Short and warm, no verb needed in Lithuanian; jūsų holds the polite address, and viskas covers the whole grid of new room.

S19.s: Ačiū, kad įsigijote. Taip palaikote Cutling ir žmogų, kuris jį kuria vienas.
S19.back: Thanks, that you-acquired. Thus you-support Cutling and the-person, who it makes alone.
S19.why: Įsigyti is the polite everyday verb for buying; the second sentence names the one person behind the app without making it a plea.

S20.s: Sveiki sugrįžę. Jūsų ankstesnis pirkinys atkurtas.
S20.back: Welcome having-returned [plural]. Your earlier purchase [is] restored.
S20.why: Sveiki sugrįžę is the fixed Lithuanian welcome back, plural for jūs; atkurtas repeats the verb from the S12 link, so the person sees it worked.

S21.back: Used [impersonal neuter] 3 out-of 5 free Cutlings [genitive plural].
S21.why: Same as S5 on purpose: VoiceOver says what the subtitle shows, and the impersonal participle reads cleanly aloud for any count.

S22.why: Genitive plural label with a colon is the Lithuanian count form that stays correct for 1, 2, 5 and 21 alike (no noun agrees with the number); telpa is the plain word for what fits.

S23.s: Cutling atrakintas. Dabar telpa iki %@ Cutlingų.
S23.back: Cutling [is] unlocked. Now fits up-to 5 000 Cutlings [genitive plural].
S23.why: Masculine participle agrees with Cutling, which the vocabulary treats as masculine (skirtas Mac); the genitive plural is right after a round thousand.

S24.why: States what happened without a subject to blame; calmer than nepavyko, which reads as a failure.

S25.s: Šiuo metu nepavyksta pasiekti „App Store“. Netrukus pabandykite dar kartą.
S25.back: At-this time it-is-not-succeeding to-reach "App Store". Shortly try [polite] one more time.
S25.why: Impersonal nepavyksta puts the fault on the connection, not the person; „App Store“ is in quotes and left undeclined, as the vocabulary writes „Apple“.

S26.why: A negated verb takes the genitive in Lithuanian, so šio pirkimo; one plain sentence.

S27.s: Šiame įrenginyje naudojamoje „Apple“ paskyroje Cutling pirkinių nerasta.
S27.back: In-this device being-used "Apple" account Cutling purchases [genitive] not-found.
S27.why: Impersonal nerasta with the genitive is how Lithuanian reports that nothing exists; naudojamoje names the account signed in here without a long clause. 73 characters.

S28.s: Nemokamoje versijoje telpa %lld Cutlingai. Atrakinę Cutling vieną kartą, išsaugosite kiek tik norite.
S28.back: In-the-free version fit 5 Cutlings [nominative plural]. Having-unlocked Cutling one time, you-will-save as-many just you-want.
S28.why: Nominative plural after 5 is correct; the participle atrakinę ties the one-time unlock to the result in one sentence, as a Lithuanian would say it to Siri's listener.

S29.why: Sits under the Cutlingai title, so the noun is left out; iš with the genitive plural works for any total from 2 up. 15 characters.

K1.why: Nominative plural participle agrees with the unspoken Cutlingai; the closing imperative is the tap target's call to act. 38 characters with the digit.

M1.why: Lithuanian Mac commands and window names are infinitives (Atidaryti, Išsaugoti); Cutling undeclined as in the vocabulary.

M2.why: The same command as M1 with the ellipsis character, because it opens a window.

M3.why: Plain noun phrase with the vocabulary's plural Cutlingai as a settings label.

M4.why: The usual Lithuanian compact pair; iš reads more naturally than a slash in a settings value.

M5.why: Masculine participle agrees with Cutling; a status, not a sentence, so no full stop.

M6.s: Vienu pirkimu atrakinsite Cutling iPhone, iPad ir Mac įrenginiuose.
M6.back: With-one purchase you-will-unlock Cutling in iPhone, iPad and Mac devices.
M6.why: Instrumental vienu pirkimu says by what means in two words; įrenginiuose carries the locative so the brand names stay as written.

M7.s: Cutling atrakintas iPhone, iPad ir Mac įrenginiuose su šia „Apple“ paskyra.
M7.back: Cutling [is] unlocked in iPhone, iPad and Mac devices with this "Apple" account.
M7.why: Mirrors M6 so the two lines read as before and after; „Apple“ paskyra as in the vocabulary, instrumental after su.

M8.s: Įsigijote Cutling, kai jis dar buvo mokamas, todėl jums jis lieka atrakintas. Ačiū už palaikymą.
M8.back: You-acquired Cutling, when it still was paid-for, therefore for-you it stays unlocked. Thanks for support.
M8.why: Gives the reason first and the result second, the order a Lithuanian explains in; the thanks avoids a gendered adjective, which polite jūs would otherwise need.
